title: X9C-2R Service Blocker Preflight Inventory

high_priority.impact: Service directly calls legacy auth-guard, violates canonical auth pattern
high_priority.refactoring_scope: Remove auth-guard import, accept capability/access parameters from routes
Remove auth-guard import, accept parameters from routes

medium_priority.current_pattern: Services accept authContext: CanonicalAuthContext parameter but only use limited fields
medium_priority.description: engagement.ts functions like getEngagementById(id, workspaceId, hasInternalAccess) and listEngagements(..., hasInternalAccess) correctly accept hasInternalAccess as parameter instead of ctx.policy

medium_priority.current_pattern: Services accept authContext parameter, use hasInternalAccess parameter for filtering
medium_priority.description: getClientById(id, workspaceId, hasInternalAccess) and listClients(..., hasInternalAccess) correctly use parameters

low_priority_or_design_dependent.description: Services that implement custom role resolution, workspace membership checks, or intervention state logic

must_refactor_in_x9c3.from_pattern: Service imports requireCapabilityForService, calls withAuth-style validation internally
must_refactor_in_x9c3.to_pattern: Route validates capability, passes capability boolean/status to service
must_refactor_in_x9c3.test_impact: Service tests must update to pass capability parameters
Multiple service tests need parameter updates

already_refactored_no_action.reason: Functions already accept hasInternalAccess as parameter
Functions already accept hasInternalAccess as parameter

expected_reduction_if_resolved.reason: Only the 4 services with auth-guard imports are addressed in X9C-3. Other 450-X=370+ violations remain from routes and other infrastructure.

critical_findings.finding: 4 of 6 services with policy/auth dependencies still use legacy auth-guard imports
critical_findings.impact: These are direct blockers for route migration. Routes cannot safely migrate to canonical pattern while their services import legacy auth.
critical_findings.blocking_timeline: X9C-3 must address these before X9C-4 route migration

critical_findings.finding: 2 services (engagement.ts, client-account.ts) are already correctly refactored
critical_findings.impact: These show the correct pattern - accept parameters instead of ctx. Can be used as templates for refactoring others.
critical_findings.positive: Proof that refactoring is feasible and maintainable

critical_findings.finding: Service refactoring is NOT just removing imports - it's changing function signatures
critical_findings.impact: All callers (routes and other services) must be updated. This is a larger scope than just X9C-3.
critical_findings.scope: Service refactoring impacts routes (X9C-4), services (X9C-3), and tests (all phases)

critical_findings.finding: 5 additional services with governance logic are design-dependent
critical_findings.impact: Cannot be refactored until X9D clarifies workspace/role semantics
critical_findings.timeline: X9D must complete before these services can be safely changed

x9c3_readiness_assessment.reason: X9C-3 is described as 'service refactoring', but current blockers (4 services with auth-guard imports) require careful design: (1) How do routes pass capability/access info to services? (2) How do services validate without auth-guard? (3) What's the signature change for each function?
x9c3_readiness_assessment.prerequisite: X9C-3 should start with SERVICE BOUNDARY DESIGN before any code changes
design_questions_to_resolve: Which services need refactoring (all 4 with auth-guard imports, or only those called by migrating routes)?
What parameters should replace requireCapabilityForService calls?
How do services know whether they're being called from canonical vs legacy routes?
Should service signatures change universally or can legacy callers coexist during transition?
What's the test strategy for changed signatures?

recommendation: X9C-3 should be renamed to 'X9C-3 Service Boundary Design + Selective Refactoring' and should NOT attempt full service refactoring of all 4 services at once. Instead: (1) Design the new service boundaries, (2) Refactor engagement.ts caller patterns as template, (3) Refactor 1-2 of the 4 high-priority services as proof-of-concept, (4) Plan full rollout for X9C-4 alongside route migration.
